hook: Your donor is the hero. Your church is the guide. Get those backwards and the story falls apart.
direction: StoryBrand premise contextualized: the organization that positions itself as the hero of its own website loses the reader. Guides equip heroes. This is also just good theology of service — serve the person in front of you. Keep that note light.

facebook.text:
Your donor is the hero. Your church is the guide. Get those backwards and the story falls apart.

Most church and nonprofit websites lead with the organization — its history, its programs, its vision. That's understandable. You're proud of the work. But the person reading your page isn't looking for a hero to admire. They're looking for a guide who can help them do something that matters.

Donald Miller calls this StoryBrand. Good theology calls it service. Either way, the principle is the same: your job is to equip the person in front of you, not to impress them.
